# Canonical dataset inventory

<!-- Generated by scripts/canonical-audit.gen.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Learn and Practice use exactly twelve datasets, one identity each (`datasetId` + `datasetVersion`), with no edition or size selector. Total: **1,657,754 rows** in 93 tables. Every dataset is built by `npm run datasets:canonical` from committed extracts (real sources) or deterministic generators (synthetic), and is served as a content-hashed, immutably cached gzip SQLite file.

## Retail (`retail`, version 3.0.0)

Two years of real invoice lines from a UK online gift wholesaler: customers, products, sales, cancellations and returns, with modeled payments and customer segment history.

- **Kind:** hybrid. **Publisher:** Daqing Chen, UCI Machine Learning Repository. **Source:** https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/502/online+retail+ii
- **Release:** Online Retail II (2019), worksheets Year 2009-2010 and Year 2010-2011
- **Licence:** CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Chen, D. (2012). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Modified by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> retail && node datasets/acquire/retail.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs retail` (seed 20251)
- **Coverage:** 2009-12-01 to 2011-12-09, grain: invoice line
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/retail-73bec4b6850b.sqlite.gz`, 12.5 MB SQLite, 3.9 MB gzip, SHA-256 `73bec4b6850b92b2775c968c01f62663eff0a8147347551bb30e0e5ac7adc0b6`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| categories | 17 | 3 | One product category (for example Christmas or Kitchen). Products are grouped into these from their descriptions. |
| products | 5,304 | 6 | One product in the catalog (one stock code). Some products never appear on invoices in this sample. |
| customers | 848 | 4 | One known customer. Anonymous (walk-in) invoices have no matching customer row. |
| orders | 6,722 | 6 | One invoice: a sale, a cancellation (credit note), or an accounting adjustment. |
| order_items | 125,613 | 7 | One line on an invoice. Cancellation lines use negative quantities. |
| payments | 5,423 | 6 | One payment attempt for a sale invoice. Payments are modeled; the original source has no payment ledger. |
| returns | 1,996 | 6 | One cancelled invoice line, linked to the earlier sale it reverses when that sale is in the data. |
| customer_history | 1,685 | 7 | One version of a customer’s segment and country over time. A new row starts when either changes. |

**Transformations**

- All invoice lines for a deterministic 14% sample of customers (FNV-1a hash of customer id) and the same share of anonymous invoices, Dec 2009 – Dec 2011.
- Overlapping worksheet dates (2010-12-01..09) are taken once, from the second worksheet.
- One order header per invoice number (earliest line timestamp); order_type from the invoice prefix.
- Product catalog covers every stock code in the full source; description and list price are the modal recorded values.
- Categories are derived from product descriptions; products with no description stay uncategorised.
- returns links each cancellation line to the latest earlier sale of that code to that customer.
- customer_history derives segment from trailing-12-month net sales at each month start.
- payments are modeled by Runtime (seed 20251): the source contains no payment ledger.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Cancellation invoices with negative quantities
- Anonymous invoices without a customer
- Repeated identical invoice lines
- Zero-price adjustment lines and non-merchandise codes (postage, fees, samples)
- Products never bought by the sampled customers
- Undescribed products with no category
- Returns with no matching earlier sale
- Unpaid sale invoices, failed attempts and split payments
- Customers whose segment or country changes over time

**Quality notes for learners**

- Net sales are quantity × unit_price summed over sale and cancellation lines; payments are a separate modeled ledger.
- Timestamps are recorded local times with an unspecified time zone.
- A 14% customer sample is not a full-company total; compare shares and trends, not absolute company revenue.
- Line descriptions can differ from catalog descriptions for the same stock code.

## U.S. Flights (`flights`, version 3.0.0)

Every domestic flight flown by a sample of 435 aircraft in January–March 2025: schedules, delays, cancellations, diversions and delay causes.

- **Kind:** real. **Publisher:** U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics; OurAirports. **Source:** https://www.transtats.bts.gov/DL_SelectFields.aspx?gnoyr_VQ=FGJ&QO_fu146_anzr=b0-gvzr
- **Release:** Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present), January–March 2025; OurAirports airports.csv retrieved 2026-10-14
- **Licence:** U.S. government work (public domain); OurAirports data is public domain (https://www.bts.gov/policies-and-notices); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Source: U.S. Bureau of Transportation Statistics, Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance. Airport names and coordinates: OurAirports (ourairports.com). Modified by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> flights && node datasets/acquire/flights.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs flights`
- **Coverage:** 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31, grain: flight leg
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/flights-27d669d55ba4.sqlite.gz`, 24.5 MB SQLite, 6.2 MB gzip, SHA-256 `27d669d55ba421f6c3edf738468de2a01df22385f6b2b10ff0bd5ae8ee04d035`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| airlines | 14 | 3 | One airline. |
| airports | 326 | 8 | One airport that appears in this dataset. |
| routes | 5,436 | 4 | One flight path from an origin airport to a destination airport. |
| calendar | 90 | 10 | One calendar date in the first quarter of 2025. |
| cancellation_reasons | 4 | 2 | One reason a flight can be cancelled (for example weather or carrier). |
| flights | 124,460 | 25 | One scheduled domestic flight, including cancelled and diverted flights. |

**Transformations**

- All flights of a deterministic 7.5% sample of aircraft (FNV-1a hash of tail number); flights without a tail number sampled by carrier, flight number and date.
- Selected 25 of 110 source fields; diversion detail fields are omitted.
- Clock times combined with the flight date; actual times are scheduled time plus reported delay minutes.
- Scheduled arrival date chosen so local arrival is closest to departure plus scheduled elapsed time.
- Airport names and coordinates joined from OurAirports by IATA code; carrier names and groups added by Runtime.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Cancelled flights with NULL actual times and delays
- Diverted flights with a departure but no arrival delay
- Early departures and arrivals (negative delays)
- Overnight flights arriving the next calendar day
- Local times in different time zones at origin and destination
- Delay causes reported only for arrivals 15+ minutes late
- Flights without a reported tail number
- Holidays and weekends in the calendar

**Quality notes for learners**

- Times are local; subtracting departure from arrival across time zones does not give duration. Use air_time_minutes.
- A cancelled flight has unknown delay, not zero delay.
- The sample is of aircraft, so carrier shares reflect the sampled fleet as well as schedules.

## Product / SaaS Analytics (`saas`, version 3.0.0)

Eighteen months of a fictional collaboration product: workspaces, users, invitations, projects, sessions, raw event deliveries, experiments, plan changes and billing.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school
- **Release:** Runtime SaaS generator 3.0.0, seed 20252
- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs saas` (seed 20252)
- **Coverage:** 2024-01-01 to 2025-06-30, grain: event delivery
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/saas-b6d53edf8ea4.sqlite.gz`, 31.2 MB SQLite, 8.1 MB gzip, SHA-256 `b6d53edf8ea464a698cf8f5018885d9b887086d6e7ac0146fce2494209517dea`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| accounts | 3,200 | 7 | One customer workspace (a company or team). |
| users | 11,348 | 9 | One person in one workspace. |
| subscriptions | 4,583 | 8 | One plan period for a workspace. Each workspace has exactly one current plan (no end date). |
| sessions | 47,891 | 5 | One product session by one user. |
| events | 135,428 | 8 | One product event as received. Retries can repeat the same event, and some events arrive late. |
| projects | 9,962 | 6 | One project created in a workspace. |
| invitations | 6,450 | 7 | One invitation sent from a workspace. |
| experiments | 20 | 6 | One product experiment. |
| experiment_assignments | 14,939 | 4 | One user’s assigned experiment variant, recorded the first time they see it. |
| billing_events | 4,193 | 6 | One billing charge or credit for a paid subscription. |

**Transformations**

- Workspace fit drives activation, team growth, session frequency, upgrades and churn; exceptions are sampled, not removed.
- Five of twenty experiments carry a real effect on their primary metric; one has an intentional 55/45 allocation; one has three arms.
- About 2.5% of client events are retried (repeated event_id), 4% arrive minutes to hours late and 1% arrive days late.
- About 1.2% of project creations have no project_created event (tracking loss).

**Intentional edge cases**

- Retried deliveries with duplicate event_id
- Late and out-of-order deliveries (received_at long after occurred_at)
- Server-side events with no session
- Projects with no creation event
- Invitations never accepted; users who joined without an invitation
- Referral relationships between users in different workspaces
- Cancellations followed by reactivation
- Annual and monthly billing; failed payments and partial refunds
- Unequal experiment allocation and a three-arm test
- Users who never return after signup

**Quality notes for learners**

- Count logical events with DISTINCT event_id; count deliveries only for pipeline questions.
- Use occurred_at for behavior and received_at for ingestion questions.
- mrr_cents is list price per month, not cash collected; billing_events records cash.

## Mobility (`mobility`, version 3.0.0)

A 1-in-87 sample of New York City yellow taxi trips from January–March 2025: pickup and drop-off zones, distances, fares, tips, fees and payment types.

- **Kind:** real. **Publisher:** New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC). **Source:** https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
- **Release:** Yellow Taxi Trip Records, January–March 2025 (Parquet); taxi zone lookup table
- **Licence:** NYC Open Data Terms of Use (free to use, including commercial use, without restriction) (https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/overview/#termsofuse); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Source: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission, TLC Trip Record Data. Modified by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> mobility && node datasets/acquire/mobility.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs mobility`
- **Coverage:** 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-31, grain: taxi trip
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/mobility-954fccdc4036.sqlite.gz`, 20.1 MB SQLite, 5.1 MB gzip, SHA-256 `954fccdc403626f098e04a2a72987ba8b40495a1c208dfe1dde0de5a50a28eca`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| boroughs | 8 | 2 | One New York City borough, plus labels for unknown and outside-NYC locations. |
| zones | 265 | 5 | One taxi pickup/dropoff zone in New York City. |
| vendors | 4 | 2 | One system that recorded the trip data. |
| payment_types | 7 | 3 | One way a trip can be paid (for example card or cash). |
| rate_codes | 7 | 2 | One taxi fare type (for example standard, JFK, or negotiated). |
| calendar | 90 | 7 | One calendar date in the first quarter of 2025. |
| trips | 128,620 | 19 | One yellow taxi trip from January–March 2025. |

**Transformations**

- Deterministic ~1.15% sample of trip records (FNV-1a hash of month and source row number).
- extra, mta_tax and improvement_surcharge combined into surcharge_amount; all other amounts kept as recorded.
- Timestamps written as NYC local clock time; records outside the file month are kept as published.
- Borough names normalised into a boroughs table; code lists from the TLC data dictionary.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Flex-fare trips with NULL passenger count and rate code
- Negative fares on reversals and disputes
- Zero-distance trips
- Cash trips record no tip
- Unknown and outside-NYC zones
- Congestion Relief Zone fee starting 5 January 2025
- A pickup timestamp outside the published month

**Quality notes for learners**

- Cash tips are not recorded, so tip rates should be measured on card trips.
- trip_distance_miles is the meter distance, not a straight line between zones.
- This is a sample; multiply counts by roughly 87 to estimate citywide volume.

## Weather (`weather`, version 3.0.0)

Three years (2022–2024) of daily observations from 100 NOAA weather stations serving 96 U.S. cities: temperatures, rain, snow and wind.

- **Kind:** real. **Publisher:** NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI); U.S. Census Bureau. **Source:** https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/land-based-station/global-historical-climatology-network-daily
- **Release:** GHCN-Daily via the NCEI Access Data Service (daily-summaries), retrieved 2026-10-14; 2023 Census Gazetteer places
- **Licence:** U.S. government work (public domain) (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/access/metadata/landing-page/bin/iso?id=gov.noaa.ncdc:C00861); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Source: NOAA NCEI Global Historical Climatology Network – Daily (Menne et al., 2012). City coordinates: U.S. Census Bureau Gazetteer. Modified by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> weather && node datasets/acquire/weather.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs weather`
- **Coverage:** 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31, grain: station-day
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/weather-d5277caf53ae.sqlite.gz`, 13.1 MB SQLite, 2.6 MB gzip, SHA-256 `d5277caf53ae8c51196ccd3d8c190ab6bddb46b828196891427332a1b26f49e9`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| states | 51 | 4 | One U.S. state or the District of Columbia. |
| cities | 96 | 6 | One city with weather coverage, including its map location. |
| stations | 100 | 10 | One weather station (usually at an airport). A city can have more than one station. |
| calendar | 1,096 | 10 | One calendar date, 2022–2024. |
| daily_weather | 109,214 | 10 | One day of weather for one station. If a station did not report that day, there is no row. |

**Transformations**

- One first-order station nearest each listed city (within 60 km) with complete TMAX, TMIN and PRCP coverage; extra stations for multi-airport metros.
- Seven elements pivoted to one row per station-day, metric units (TAVG is not published for these stations).
- Values with a NOAA quality-control flag set to NULL; trace precipitation recorded as 0 mm with precip_trace = 1.
- Census regions and divisions, and a 2022–2024 calendar, added by Runtime.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Days with no row for a station (gaps in the date series)
- Measurements a station does not report at all (snow at southern stations)
- Trace precipitation (0 mm but not dry)
- Values removed by NOAA quality control
- Cities with several stations
- Leap day 2024-02-29
- Extremes: desert heat, Alaska cold, hurricane rainfall

**Quality notes for learners**

- NULL means not reported or failed quality control; it is not zero.
- Stations represent airports or observation sites, not citywide averages.
- Three years are weather, not a climate trend.

## Energy (`energy`, version 3.0.0)

Hourly electricity demand, forecasts, generation and interchange for twelve major U.S. balancing authorities, January–June 2024, with daily fuel mix and flows between neighbouring grids.

- **Kind:** real. **Publisher:** U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). **Source:** https://www.eia.gov/electricity/gridmonitor/
- **Release:** EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor six-month files, 2024 January–June; EIA-930 reference tables
- **Licence:** U.S. government work (public domain) (https://www.eia.gov/about/copyrights_reuse.php); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-930 Hourly Electric Grid Monitor. Modified by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> energy && node datasets/acquire/energy.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs energy`
- **Coverage:** 2024-01-01 to 2024-06-30, grain: balancing authority hour
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/energy-7b472c47f74e.sqlite.gz`, 14.9 MB SQLite, 3.6 MB gzip, SHA-256 `7b472c47f74e73aead19f28a45cd2a5746abd891d79c912c0faedd5473b0478f`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| regions | 15 | 4 | One power-grid region or neighbouring country. |
| balancing_authorities | 62 | 6 | One grid operator (balancing authority). Twelve have hourly detail; the rest appear only as interchange partners. |
| fuel_types | 9 | 5 | One energy source used for generation (for example coal, natural gas, or wind). |
| calendar | 182 | 7 | One calendar date, January–June 2024. |
| hourly_demand | 52,405 | 9 | One hour for one grid operator: electricity demand and the day-ahead forecast. |
| generation | 52,405 | 15 | One hour for one grid operator: power generated, power traded with neighbours, and generation by fuel. |
| generation_by_fuel | 15,824 | 5 | One day for one grid operator and one fuel: total generation that day. |
| interchange | 17,654 | 5 | One day of scheduled power flow from one grid operator to another. |

**Transformations**

- Twelve balancing authorities kept at hourly grain: BPAT, CISO, DUK, ERCO, FPL, ISNE, MISO, NYIS, PJM, SOCO, SWPP, TVA.
- As-reported values only; EIA imputed and adjusted series are omitted, so missing hours stay NULL.
- Fuel mix and BA-to-BA interchange summed to the reporting BA’s local date, with hours_reported.
- Timestamps converted from M/D/YYYY h:mm AM/PM to ISO-style text.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Missing demand, forecast and interchange hours (NULL)
- Daylight-saving days with 23 or 25 local hours
- Negative net generation for pumped storage and station use
- Interchange reported by one side only; partners outside the twelve hourly BAs
- Canadian and Mexican interchange partners
- Generation-only balancing authorities

**Quality notes for learners**

- MW over one hour equals MWh; daily totals are sums of hourly MW.
- Demand ≈ net generation − total interchange; reported values do not always balance.
- Local hours repeat or skip at daylight-saving changes; use hour_ending_utc for ordering.

## Finance / Payments (`payments`, version 3.0.0)

Six months of a fictional bank: customers, checking, savings and credit-card accounts, cards, merchants, card authorizations and settlements, refunds, disputes and the account ledger.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school
- **Release:** Runtime payments generator 3.0.0, seed 20253
- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs payments` (seed 20253)
- **Coverage:** 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30, grain: ledger entry; card authorization
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/payments-235305081588.sqlite.gz`, 22.7 MB SQLite, 6.0 MB gzip, SHA-256 `235305081588686f23eff715d21798a80d3ef23ed615781d865024138c5f926d`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| customers | 1,120 | 7 | One fictional retail-banking customer. |
| accounts | 2,109 | 7 | One deposit or credit-card account owned by one customer. |
| cards | 1,774 | 8 | One payment card. Lost or expired cards are replaced by a new card on the same account. |
| merchants | 1,014 | 6 | One card-accepting merchant location. |
| authorizations | 40,508 | 10 | One card authorization request. The same request can appear more than once when the network retries. |
| settlements | 37,071 | 4 | One completed card purchase. The final amount can differ from the authorization (tips, hotels, currency conversion). |
| refunds | 1,230 | 5 | One merchant refund against a settlement; a settlement can have several partial refunds. |
| chargebacks | 199 | 7 | One cardholder dispute against a settlement. |
| transactions | 84,798 | 12 | One money movement on an account. Negative amounts are money out. Pending entries have no posted time yet. |

**Transformations**

- Each customer’s accounts are simulated in time order: holds, available balance, declines, settlements, overdrafts and refunds follow from the running balance.
- Payroll, rent, utilities, subscriptions, savings transfers, card payments and interest recur on realistic schedules.
- Merchant category codes follow ISO 18245; names, people and amounts are fictional.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Declines for insufficient funds, credit limit, fraud, frozen and expired cards
- Duplicate approvals from network retries (shared request_key) that never settle
- Settled amounts different from authorized amounts (tips, fuel, hotels, currency)
- Merchant voids (reversed) and purchases still pending at the end of the period
- Partial and multiple refunds; disputes credited, rejected or open
- Overdrafts and overdraft fees
- Recurring charges with mid-period price increases
- Lost cards replaced on the same account
- Settlements with no ledger posting and manual ledger adjustments

**Quality notes for learners**

- All money is integer US cents except authorization amounts, which are in the transaction currency.
- Authorizations are requests, not money movement; only posted ledger entries change balances.
- Balance at time t = opening_balance_cents + SUM(amount_cents) of posted entries with posted_at <= t.

## Healthcare (`healthcare`, version 3.0.0)

Three years of synthetic patient journeys: patients, clinicians, appointments, visits, diagnoses, prescriptions, vital signs, lab results and procedures. No real person’s health information is present.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school
- **Release:** Runtime healthcare generator 3.0.0, seed 20254
- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime. Diagnosis codes are ICD-10-CM (U.S. public domain); procedure and measurement codes are Runtime-defined.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs healthcare` (seed 20254)
- **Coverage:** 2022-07-01 to 2025-06-30, grain: encounter; observation
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/healthcare-d3c46337ab78.sqlite.gz`, 12.9 MB SQLite, 3.4 MB gzip, SHA-256 `d3c46337ab78a10bf0bc6a27bc2bc7bbc014864e97d721467046181dc6745e9c`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| patients | 3,200 | 9 | One fictional patient. |
| providers | 460 | 6 | One clinician. |
| encounters | 20,447 | 9 | One patient visit (clinic, telehealth, urgent care, emergency, or hospital stay). |
| appointments | 19,438 | 7 | One booked appointment. Completed appointments link to the visit they produced. |
| conditions | 8,563 | 7 | One diagnosis recorded for a patient. Chronic conditions have no resolved date. |
| medications | 19,275 | 8 | One prescription fill period. Repeat fills of the same drug can overlap or leave gaps. |
| observations | 39,529 | 8 | One measurement: vital sign or lab result. |
| procedures | 8,482 | 7 | One procedure, test or vaccination performed during an encounter. |

**Transformations**

- Age and frailty drive chronic-condition prevalence; conditions drive follow-up visits, labs and medications.
- Chronic medications are 180-day supplies renewed early (overlapping intervals) or late (gaps in therapy).
- Appointments can be cancelled and rebooked, missed (no-show) or still scheduled after the data ends.
- Emergency visits can lead to inpatient stays and 30-day readmissions.
- Modeled after the concepts of Synthea; no Synthea output or real patient data is used.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Patients with no encounters; providers who never saw a patient
- Cancelled, no-show and future-scheduled appointments with no encounter
- Overlapping and gapped medication fill intervals
- Ongoing chronic conditions with NULL resolved dates
- Measurements attempted but not obtained (NULL value)
- Inpatient stays spanning several days; 30-day readmissions
- Patients who died during the period
- Telehealth visits without vital signs

**Quality notes for learners**

- All people and clinicians are fictional; prevalence and costs are illustrative, not epidemiological estimates.
- stop_date is exclusive: a fill covers start_date up to the day before stop_date.
- Use the patient’s age at the visit, not today, for age-based analysis.

## IoT / Sensors (`iot`, version 3.0.0)

Two months of telemetry from sensors across eight fictional facilities: cold rooms, freezers, production lines, offices and pump stations, with alerts, outages and maintenance.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school

- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs iot` (seed 20255)
- **Coverage:** 2025-03-01 to 2025-04-30, grain: sensor reading
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/iot-6060a8f96234.sqlite.gz`, 19.6 MB SQLite, 4.3 MB gzip, SHA-256 `6060a8f962345fa3b45bb210a7978e07b832288e2d095c562d9f8857d30ec4b2`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| locations | 41 | 5 | One monitored zone inside a site. |
| sensor_types | 10 | 7 | One kind of measurement (for example temperature), including valid ranges and alert thresholds. |
| devices | 186 | 9 | One installed sensor device. |
| sensor_readings | 150,425 | 10 | One sensor reading. The same reading can arrive more than once when a device retransmits. |
| alerts | 483 | 7 | One alert period when a device went out of range or lost connectivity. |
| maintenance | 168 | 7 | One maintenance visit for a device. Two technicians can log overlapping orders for the same visit. |
| device_status_events | 1,231 | 5 | One change in a device’s status. That status lasts until the next status event. |

**Transformations**

- Signals follow physical patterns: defrost cycles, occupancy-driven CO2, working-hours power, vibration drift before failures, battery discharge.
- Alerts are derived from the readings with hysteresis; status events and maintenance follow outages and failures.
- Network outages buffer readings and deliver them late; power outages lose them; about 1% of messages are retransmitted.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Gaps in readings during outages and dropped messages
- Late batches delivered after a network outage (received_at ≫ recorded_at)
- Retransmitted duplicates with the same sequence_number
- Fault readings: NULL values and physically impossible values
- Threshold violations forming consecutive runs (islands)
- Overlapping maintenance work orders for the same device
- Devices installed or retired during the period; spares that never reported
- Status changes recorded only when the state changes (fill-forward needed)

**Quality notes for learners**

- Order by recorded_at for physical analysis and by received_at for pipeline analysis.
- Deduplicate on (device_id, sequence_number) before counting readings.
- Exclude values outside the sensor type’s valid range before averaging.

## Logistics (`logistics`, version 3.0.0)

Four months of a fictional parcel network: shipments and packages moving from fulfillment centers through sortation hubs to delivery stations, with every scan, delivery attempt and return.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school
- **Release:** Runtime logistics generator 3.0.0, seed 20256
- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs logistics` (seed 20256)
- **Coverage:** 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-30, grain: tracking event
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/logistics-789cfa035c73.sqlite.gz`, 18.7 MB SQLite, 4.6 MB gzip, SHA-256 `789cfa035c733ee1ab50e146dbab019db2b1dc34e8a328909af81f0cf8cde766`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| service_levels | 8 | 5 | One shipping service with its delivery promise. |
| carriers | 14 | 4 | One fictional transport carrier. |
| warehouses | 38 | 6 | One facility in the network: fulfillment center, sort hub, or delivery station. |
| routes | 173 | 6 | One scheduled truck lane between two facilities. |
| shipments | 8,200 | 12 | One customer order shipped as one or more packages. |
| packages | 11,505 | 8 | One physical package within a shipment. |
| tracking_events | 100,515 | 9 | One package scan or status update. Scans can repeat, go missing, arrive late, or show up out of order. |
| delivery_attempts | 12,700 | 6 | One attempt by a driver to deliver a package. |

**Transformations**

- Each package follows a physical path: pickup, origin departure, one or two hubs, delivery station, out for delivery, attempts.
- About 5% of intermediate scans are missing, 3.5% of scanner events repeat, carrier API events arrive in delayed batches.
- Failed attempts are retried on business days; three failures, a refusal or damage return the package to sender.
- Shipper names, tracking numbers and postal codes are entered inconsistently on purpose.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Duplicate scans of the same step
- Missing intermediate scans
- Late, batched and out-of-order ingestion (recorded_at)
- A scan recorded after delivery (out_for_delivery after delivered)
- Reroutes to a different delivery station
- Failed attempts, returns to sender and lost packages
- Packages still in transit at the end of the data
- Messy shipper names, tracking numbers and postal codes

**Quality notes for learners**

- The latest state of a package is its most recent event by event_at, not by event_id.
- Normalize tracking numbers with UPPER and REPLACE before matching.
- promised_delivery_date counts business days from label creation.

## Developer Platform (`developer`, version 3.0.0)

Eighteen months of activity on a fictional code-hosting platform: organizations, nested teams, developers and managers, repositories and forks, pull requests, reviews, commits, issues, deployments and incidents.

- **Kind:** synthetic. **Publisher:** Runtime. **Source:** https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school
- **Release:** Runtime developer-platform generator 3.0.0, seed 20257
- **Licence:** Runtime-owned synthetic data (https://github.com/KrishnaSathvik/runtime.school); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** Synthetic data generated by Runtime.
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/build.mjs developer` (seed 20257)
- **Coverage:** 2024-01-01 to 2025-06-30, grain: commit; pull request; deployment
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/developer-a8e805541be6.sqlite.gz`, 12.5 MB SQLite, 4.9 MB gzip, SHA-256 `a8e805541be668c7c9590a4acabbac3a3cb6d9b49451aba1a7cec1ca466c8027`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| organizations | 60 | 5 | One customer organization on the developer platform. |
| teams | 324 | 4 | One team inside an organization. Teams can nest under other teams. |
| developers | 2,891 | 9 | One person with an account in an organization. |
| repositories | 512 | 9 | One code repository. Forks point to the repository they were copied from. |
| pull_requests | 13,242 | 10 | One pull request. |
| commits | 35,881 | 9 | One code commit. Each commit can point to the previous commit on its branch. |
| reviews | 19,622 | 5 | One review submitted on a pull request. |
| issues | 7,214 | 9 | One tracked issue. |
| deployments | 8,991 | 8 | One deployment of a commit to an environment. |
| incidents | 270 | 8 | One production incident. |

**Transformations**

- Organizations have nested teams (up to four levels) and a management chain from VP to engineers.
- Repository activity drives pull requests; reviewers come from the owning team; merged PRs advance the commit chain and can be deployed.
- Rolled-back production deployments can open incidents; other incidents have no deployment cause.

**Intentional edge cases**

- Team hierarchy up to four levels; management chains of different depth
- Developers with no team; repositories with no owning team
- Forks referencing their source repository
- Commits with no linked author (bots, unlinked emails) and direct pushes without a PR
- Pull requests with no reviews, several reviews, or changes requested then approved
- Open pull requests and issues at the end of the data
- Failed and rolled-back deployments; incidents with and without a deployment cause
- Developers who left during the period

**Quality notes for learners**

- Review time is measured from pull_requests.created_at to the first review’s submitted_at.
- A developer can author and review in the same repository but never reviews their own pull request.
- Deployment frequency and change failure rate are computed on production deployments.

## Sports (`sports`, version 3.0.0)

Ten seasons of Major League Baseball results (2016–2025) with every 2025 player batting line, rosters, ballparks and month-end standings.

- **Kind:** real. **Publisher:** Retrosheet. **Source:** https://www.retrosheet.org/downloads/csvdownloads.html
- **Release:** Retrosheet CSV downloads: gameinfo (1897–2025), 2025 season files, biographical files
- **Licence:** Retrosheet notice: free use including commercial products, provided the Retrosheet statement appears prominently (https://www.retrosheet.org/notice.txt); commercial reuse: permitted.
- **Attribution:** The information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet. Interested parties may contact Retrosheet at "www.retrosheet.org".
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-14. **Reproduce:** `node datasets/acquire/download.mjs <dir> sports && node datasets/acquire/sports.mjs <dir> && node datasets/build.mjs sports`
- **Coverage:** 2016-04-03 to 2025-11-01, grain: game; player batting line (2025)
- **Asset:** `/datasets/canonical/sports-3d8dbe4b7eec.sqlite.gz`, 11.4 MB SQLite, 2.7 MB gzip, SHA-256 `3d8dbe4b7eec25b05b85f2150d7fee1425e7ac76270e520e80b6d23adf47438d`

| Table | Rows | Columns | Grain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| teams | 31 | 6 | One MLB team. The Athletics appear twice: Oakland (OAK) through 2024, then Sacramento (ATH) in 2025. |
| venues | 48 | 5 | One ballpark that hosted a game, including neutral and international sites. |
| seasons | 10 | 5 | One MLB season. |
| games | 23,168 | 13 | One completed regular-season or postseason game. |
| players | 1,471 | 9 | One player who appeared in a 2025 MLB game. |
| player_game_stats | 73,029 | 17 | One player’s batting stats in one 2025 game. Pitchers usually appear with zero plate appearances. |
| standings | 2,010 | 7 | One team’s win–loss record at the end of a month (and at season end). |

**Transformations**

- Regular-season and postseason games 2016–2025; All-Star games excluded.
- 2025 batting lines with stattype = value; a player re-entering one game is summed to one line.
- Players are all 2025 roster entries; primary position is the position with the most 2025 games.
- League and division assignments, the Rays nickname and venue countries added by Runtime.
- Seasons and month-end standings derived from game results.

**Intentional edge cases**

- A relocated franchise with two team codes (OAK → ATH)
- The shortened 60-game 2020 season played mostly without fans (NULL attendance)
- Doubleheaders on the same date
- Neutral and international sites (London, Tokyo, Seoul, Mexico City, Field of Dreams)
- Pitchers with batting lines of zero plate appearances
- Ties in wins, runs and player totals
- Substitutes without a recorded lineup slot

**Quality notes for learners**

- Player batting lines cover 2025 only; game results cover ten seasons.
- Standings are cumulative to each snapshot date; differences between snapshots give monthly records.
- A team appears in two rows per game in player_game_stats joins only through its own players.
